data.title: How electricity gets to your outlet

sentences.text: If you run a wire from a power plant to your house, you have electricity.
But the long wire wastes power as heat and glows.
So a transformer pushes it to 100,000 volts or more, and the wire cools.
But now that voltage at your house bursts into sparks.
So a transformer on the pole steps it down.
Power flows down the wire, and the porch light comes on.
But a storm drops a branch on the line, and the lights go out.
So you bury the cable underground.
A common pole transformer turns 7,200 volts into 240.
Add a meter on the wall beside the light.
Congratulations, you have built the power grid.
